overview: Both arise from the superposition of waves, but interference involves a few discrete coherent sources while diffraction involves a continuous distribution of wavelets from one aperture/obstacle.
genZNote: Interference is a small coherent squad; diffraction is a continuous wavelet crowd, and the fringe pattern shows it.

aspects.label: Source of Waves
aspects.valueA: Superposition of waves from two (or a few) coherent, discrete sources.
aspects.valueB: Superposition of secondary wavelets from different points of the SAME wavefront (single slit/obstacle).

aspects.label: Fringe Pattern
aspects.valueA: Fringes are equally spaced and of equal (or near-equal) intensity.
aspects.valueB: A wide, bright central maximum, flanked by much dimmer, unequally spaced secondary maxima.

overlay.commonMisconception: Treating interference and diffraction as unrelated phenomena rather than both being consequences of the superposition principle.
